title: Iran fires drones at U.S. base in Bahrain, denies reports of planned dirty bomb attack in D.C.
summary: Iran fired drones at a U.S. military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday, even as talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar to end the nearly nine-month war were taking place.

image.caption: Motorbikes drive beneath a billboard depicting a launched missile as well as current and the late Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commanders on Monday in Tehran. Iran launched drones at a U.S. base in Bahrain for the second time in three days. (Vahid Salemi/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
Iran fired drones at a U.S. military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday, even as talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar to end the nearly nine-month war were taking place.
U.S., Bahrain officials indicate no casualties from Iran drone attack
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards said the radar system that it attacked was at the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain, the Arab Gulf state that is home to the U.S. Fifth Fleet.
Bahrain said it had intercepted the attack after sending an air raid alert ​and telling citizens to take shelter. There were no reports of casualties or damage.

"Multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps] today towards Bahrain were intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel," U.S. Central Command said in its own statement.

Bahrain had ​also intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks on Sunday, during which Tehran said it had targeted a U.S. radar system at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base after what it said were hostile U.S. actions.
Meanwhile, the Iranian Foreign Ministry denied a report from CNN that Tehran was ⁠developing plans ⁠to ⁠target senior members of Donald Trump's administration with a dirty bomb ​in ⁠Washington.

Trump says he will hold off on fresh Iran strikes for now

blocks.text: "The baseless allegations seeking to link Iran’s dams to missile bases constitute yet another example of a malicious campaign to manufacture propaganda and security pretexts aimed at justifying attacks on a country’s vital infrastructure," Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, said on X.
Trump was asked whether there was an "imminent threat" to Washington, while attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in Manila.
"If there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before," said Trump. "We take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy."

U.S. President Donald Trump, while standing at the Manila summit beside Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, left, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, right, warned Iran of the consequences of any attack inside the U.S. (Carlos Barria/Reuters)
Dirty bombs combine conventional explosives, such as dynamite, with radioactive material, which is dispersed by the blast.

The number of casualties and the extent of damage from a dirty bomb depends on many variables, including the weather, and the amount and type of explosives and radioactive material. Most dirty bombs would not discharge enough radiation to cause death or even severe illness.
Mixed messaging on status of war

The CNN report cited seven American officials, speaking on the condition of anonymity. The report allowed that some officials doubted whether Iran had the capability to execute such an attack. Responding to a request for comment, a White House spokesperson told CNN there was "no credible threats to the homeland."

The war has ground to a stalemate, with Trump giving mixed messaging. Last week, he said the war was "effectively over" and that he ​might hold off from attacking Iran if the U.S. does not face what he described as provocations from Tehran or ⁠the Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen.
He also publicly instructed Vice-President JD Vance to stand down from negotiating with Iranian officials to focus on domestic concerns.

But Trump has ⁠said he will maintain a U.S. naval blockade on Iran in response to ‌Tehran's continued disruption of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global energy supplies and other trade.
What Trump's midterm thumping means for the Iran war

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has averaged 10.5 million barrels of oil per day (BPD) since the start of October, according to Kpler, which tracks global shipping. While that is still below the pre-war average of 13.5 million BPD, it is up substantially from the depths of the war in the spring and late summer.

The military intervention at sea comes at a cost for the U.S., which has spent at least $40 billion on the Iran war. The war's effects on the cost of living have been cited as a factor in the significant losses Trump's Republican Party suffered in the midterm vote two weeks ago.
The disruption to shipping has threatened oil supplies ⁠and caused global economic problems.

Attacks on tankers have increased in the waterway, which carried about one-fifth of global energy supplies before the war and is a sticking point in negotiations on ending the conflict. Gulf exporters have been increasingly using workarounds to raise oil flows via Hormuz.
The United Kingdom ​Maritime Trade Operations agency said the crew of a tanker passing through the waterway was unaccounted for after being attacked north of the Omani port city of Khasab.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards said a ship carrying liquefied natural gas ⁠and an oil tanker had caught fire in the strait. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

blocks.text: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi was on Tuesday visiting Oman, which lies on the opposite side of the Strait of Hormuz to Iran and has mediated in the conflict that began with U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran on Feb. 28

Araqchi discussed safeguarding maritime corridors and ensuring the smooth flow of global ⁠shipping and trade with Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi, the Omani Foreign Ministry said. The two also talked about revitalizing channels for dialogue and negotiation to prevent escalation.

Qatar, also a key mediator between Iran and ‌the United States, said that ​it would hold ​a meeting with Iranian officials ​on Tuesday to ⁠exchange ⁠views ‌on current proposals as part of ongoing mediation ⁠efforts.
